key_reasoning.reason: New SSOSessionExpiryInterceptor follows the exact interceptor pattern used by sibling proxy plugins (e.g. sso-auth.plugin.ts) and reuses existing re-auth plumbing (startDetachedSsoLogin, markAnalyticsAuthInvalid) without modifying it, but it is authentication-flow code — it relabels an expired-session redirect as a 401 and kicks off re-auth, which is auth-sensitive and warrants the standard auth bump even though the pattern is well-established and covered by an 8-case defensive test suite (JWT no-op, confirmed-expired, still-fresh, undefined expiresAt, non-redirect 503, 303 variant, clock-skew tolerance, re-auth-plumbing failure fallback).

Single self-contained proxy plugin (SSOSessionExpiryPlugin + its interceptor) added to one existing file, registered via a one-line addition to the core plugin registry (plugins/index.ts); no other module's internals were touched.

red_flags_applied: Technical Risk bumped from S to M: affects authentication/authorization (plugin detects expired SSO session and triggers re-auth)
